summary: GRI 207 covers tax, an important source of government revenue and a key way organizations contribute to the economies where they operate. It sets out disclosures on approach to tax, tax governance, stakeholder engagement and country-by-country reporting.

questions.text: How does the organization manage tax as a material topic (GRI 3-3)?
questions.hint: Describe how the organization manages the topic and its related impacts, as required by Disclosure 3-3 in GRI 3: Material Topics 2021.

questions.text: What is the organization's approach to tax?
questions.hint: a. Description of the approach to tax: i. whether there is a tax strategy and a link if public; ii. governance body or executive position that approves it and review frequency; iii. approach to regulatory compliance; iv. link to business and sustainable development strategies.

questions.text: How are tax governance, control and risk management handled?
questions.hint: a. Tax governance and control framework: i. body or position accountable for compliance; ii. how approach to tax is embedded; iii. approach to tax risks; iv. how compliance is evaluated. b. Mechanisms to raise concerns about tax conduct and integrity. c. Assurance process for tax disclosures, with a link to any external assurance report.

questions.text: How does the organization engage stakeholders and manage their concerns related to tax?
questions.hint: a. Approach to stakeholder engagement and management of tax concerns: i. engagement with tax authorities; ii. public policy advocacy on tax; iii. processes for collecting and considering stakeholder views and concerns, including external stakeholders.

questions.text: What country-by-country tax and financial information does the organization report?
questions.hint: a. All tax jurisdictions where entities are resident for tax purposes. b. For each: resident entity names, primary activities, employees, third-party and intra-group revenues, profit/loss before tax, tangible assets, corporate income tax paid and accrued, reasons for difference from the statutory rate. c. Time period covered.
